name: offload-prefetch-declared
description: Declared experiment for Open Question 5 (when is offloading worth it?). The runner wiring is CPU-verified as a documented no-op (tests/unit/test_offload_prefetch.py), but answering the question needs a real second memory tier and a measured interconnect bandwidth, neither of which exists on the development hardware: no CUDA device, and Tier.bandwidth_gbps deliberately stays None rather than assuming a PCIe constant. Run this on a CUDA machine that can measure its own interconnect, then write the result up under Results or Failed Experiments in docs/research.md (see F15).

runs.notes: reference: no offload, no prefetch, all bytes device-resident
offload to a 0.25 MiB device ceiling, then prefetch the next layer. On a single-tier (CPU) device this is a recorded no-op; the measurement this config exists for requires CUDA.
